Intelligent Research Assistant
Project Report
8
Future Work
While the current iteration of the Intelligent Research Assistant is highly capable, several
avenues exist for future enhancement.
8.1
Hybrid Search Capabilities
Currently, the system relies exclusively on Dense Vector Search (semantic similarity).
However, dense vectors sometimes struggle with exact keyword matching (e.g., searching
for a specific serial number or a precise chemical formula).
Implementing a Hybrid
Search architecture—combining FAISS dense vector search with a sparse keyword search
index (such as BM25 via Elasticsearch)—would drastically improve recall accuracy for
highly technical queries.
8.2
Multi-Modal Analysis
Modern research is not purely textual.
Papers contain charts, graphs, and complex
mathematical formulas.
Integrating multi-modal LLMs (such as GPT-4o or LLaVA)
would allow users to ask questions like, "Summarize the data trend shown in Figure 3 of
the uploaded PDF." This requires migrating from standard text-based vector embeddings
to multimodal embeddings (like CLIP) that encode both text and image data into the
same mathematical space.
8.3
Distributed Task Queues
As user load scales, relying on FastAPI’s built-in BackgroundTasks will become a lim-
itation, as tasks are bound to the memory of the specific worker process.
Migrating
heavy document parsing and embedding tasks to a distributed queue like Celery backed
by Redis or RabbitMQ will allow the application to scale horizontally, spinning up
dedicated worker nodes exclusively for processing documents during peak upload hours.
